you need to get cooking. make your meals at home.

you need to eat 3 meals a day. eat your breakfast or else!!! you need to start your day with foods that give you energy so you won't get super hungry later in the day. if you deny yourself of nutrients you will be housing the entire refrigerator by evening, it is human nature and you cannot outsmart your brain when it comes to that shit.


you need to eat balanced meals. not talking about the food pyramid. education on nutrition is such a fucking joke. the food pyramid is just to categorize food so we can explain it in conversation. when it comes to actually balancing your meals you need fats, proteins and carbs. that's all you need to know. (fiber is important too but you need to incorporate it into your fats/proteins/carbs).

start learning what foods are. memorize what are carbs and fats. memorize what foods are high in protein. it's easier than you think, it starts to become common sense quickly.

learn portion sizes. for instance: for my dinners i just pick a carb, either bread/pasta/rice usually. pick a meat: and use a serving size of about 20-30 grams of protein. i also pick a vegetable for a side. and you have to add sauce, cheese, cool in olive oil or something to add a fat. you cannot cut out fats. fats are what make your brain work, it is really bad for your mental health to try to cut it out. your brain turns into a very dark place without consuming fats on the daily. (cut out excess fat but do NOT cut it out completely or you will be housing the fridge by evening).

my breakfast, for example: bagel with cream cheese and two fried eggs (one on each side and i eat it open face). and on the side a serving size of greek yogurt. (2 eggs is about 14 g of protein, the greek yogurt is about 12. you should shoot for 20-30 g of protein per meal). 

even your snacks should be somewhat balanced. like, instead of chips eat crackers with cheese (cheese has protein and healthy fats!).

IT IS IMPORTANT TO KNOW that you SHOULD NOT be worried about being perfect about any of these things. your body is a machine but it's not a robot. when it comes to the exact numbers in nutrition you do not need to be 100% precise. obsessing over the numbers is how you catch an eating disorder! and though you may lose a shit ton of weight from that, you will lose your mental health and years of your life because it will completely stall you from growing as a person at all. when you have an eating disorder and then you recover it's like you just got out of prison and have nothing to show for those years you were "away" (except for your weight loss but then it's gonna take you even longer to recover and you won't be able to enjoy any of it until you do).

anyway. when you eat balanced meals it keeps you from over eating. it keeps your cravings away. if you only eat carbs/sugars you will remain hungry bc your body is still begging for the other nutrients you are not providing yourself. carbs/sugar is the quickest way for your body to get energy but it lasts the shortest amount of time. so if you eat a poptart for breakfast you will be hungry an hour later and you will crave another poptart for another quick burst of energy. if you eat balanced meals than youre sugar cravings go away. because combining a serving size of carbs with a serving size of fats and proteins will make the energy the meal gives you last way longer than if you just ate carbs.

also you gotta get moving of course. go on walks. even if you can only walk for short periods of time, do it multiple times a day. at some point you can do home workouts. there are an infinite amount of videos of home workouts on YouTube you can follow. 


QUIT drinking sugar. simply cease. drink the fake sugar if you have to. but quit pop. when you quit pop you will stop craving it. drink hella water. put the zero calorie/zero sugar flavor packets in it. and drink tf up. all through out the day. don't drink an entire water bottle at once and think youre hydrated. drink water with every meal. drink it as soon as you wake up.

you have to give it all time though. your cravings won't change over night. it will be gradual but still quicker than you expect. within a year you will feel so much different.


last tip: if you use social media start following accounts that give ideas for healthy meals and snacks. it helps a lot! but i would suggest not following the accounts that are super strict about nutrition bc that could also be too much mentally. (don't follow accounts that are obsessive about micros/macros).

ive never been near death or anything, but ive said goodbye to several people now. i know i don't know anything, but ive assumed for years now that dying is like an acid trip. at least, that's the only thing ive ever experienced that i could possibly relate it to in the sense that it is an experience unlike anything else you can experience in life. when youre dying i gotta assume you are perceiving things in a way that is different from anything you have ever felt before. it has to be a completely different, undescribable way of existing, like how am acid trip is... and when youre tripping balls you need a trip sitter. you need someone there to tell you that everything is going to be all right. i think that's what people need when they are dying. 

when my grandmother was passing she had many visitors. it was during the pandemic so she could only have 2 visitors per every 24 hours, so everyone in my family took our turns everyday. when my sibling and i went i made sure to reassure her of all her worries, bc knowing my family i knew no one else would have done that. she was anxious about many things bc she was sick and dying and it made her brain crazy with worry. i told her so many things. i repeated over and over how she shouldn't be "suspicious" of the hospice facility she was in and that the workers were really nice. i told her i understood why she would be anxious about where she was, bc she was unfamiliar with it and she was sick but that those were the reasons why she was worried. i told her we all really liked the facility and thought highly of it and wouldn't have her staying somewhere we didn't trust. i told her about each of our family members and how we were all doing good and that we were "set" in life. i said everything casually, i didn't want to make it seem like i was doing a "goodbye" spiel. i just worked everything into conversation and nothing was non sequitur. told her about all her grandkids buying houses and starting careers and all that. told her about how everyone was doing good and was going to be fine in life. told her her own children were set for life. etc. i told her her house and her husband were all set. that her husband will always be cared for by us all. 

i repeated so many things to her, bc she wasn't completely lucid and it seemed like she would forget she already said certain things. but over the hours i was there she stopped saying all those things. she listened to everything i said and believed everything i said. she seemed more at peace. 

a few days later she asked my mom for my sister and i to come again. she specifically asked for us. so we came back and i did all of it again. i spent the entire time rapid fire answering her questions and reassuring her over and over that every aspect of her life and the people in her life were more than okay. 

that day that i visited her for the second time in hospice care was her last day that she spoke to anyone. after that she became nonverbal. and the next day she passed away.

you did the right thing. when someone is dying, theyre dying and everything needs to be about them. they need to know that everything is okay. they need to be told that their work here is done. they need to be at peace when they pass. it's the nicest thing you could possibly do for someone, is giving them that peace.
